title: President Murmu's Odisha Visit Put Off to November 4-5 as Cyclone Nears Coast
excerpt: The two-day Rairangpur programme planned for October 28-29 was postponed by the President's Secretariat as a Bay of Bengal storm is forecast to make landfall on the morning of October 28.
body:
• President Droupadi Murmu's two-day Odisha visit has been postponed from October 28-29 to November 4-5 because of a forecast cyclone in the Bay of Bengal.
  • The change was conveyed on Saturday by the Tour Section of the President's Secretariat; the visit has been rescheduled, not cancelled.
  • The programme centres on Rairangpur in Mayurbhanj district, the President's hometown, reached via Kalaikunda in West Bengal, with inaugurations and foundation-laying ceremonies planned.
  • The storm behind the decision is a low-pressure system expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm and make landfall on the morning of October 28 — coastal residents should follow IMD and district advisories.

President Droupadi Murmu's scheduled two-day visit to Odisha has been postponed by a week, from October 28-29 to November 4-5, as a cyclonic storm builds over the Bay of Bengal. The revised schedule was conveyed on Saturday in a letter from the Tour Section of the President's Secretariat to the authorities responsible for the arrangements.

A hometown programme, deferred

Under the original itinerary, the President was to travel to Rairangpur in Mayurbhanj district — her hometown — via Kalaikunda in West Bengal. The two days were expected to include inaugurations, foundation-laying ceremonies and public engagements. Officials have stressed that the programme itself stands; it is the dates that have moved, and arrangements will be realigned to the November schedule. Further details of the revised programme are awaited.

The storm behind the decision

The postponement follows the forecast track of a low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal that is set to intensify into a cyclonic storm, with landfall expected on the morning of October 28 — the day the visit was to begin. We have been tracking the same system's path toward the Odisha-Andhra coast in our coverage of the Bay of Bengal storm expected on October 28. A presidential visit draws district administrations, security and protocol machinery into days of preparation across the exact coastal belt a cyclone threatens; moving the visit clears that machinery for storm preparation instead.

Why a week's delay matters

Rairangpur is not a ceremonial stop chosen at random. It is where the President comes from, and visits by a head of state to a hometown carry a local weight that a Bhubaneswar programme does not: schools, civic bodies and district officials plan around the day for weeks. Postponing by a full week, rather than by a day or two, signals that the administration is planning for the storm's aftermath as well as its landfall — roads, power and communications in Mayurbhanj and the coastal districts may need days to normalise even if the cyclone weakens or veers. A shorter delay would have risked a second postponement; the November 4-5 dates put clear water between the landfall window and the visit.

What to watch

For residents of Odisha's coastal districts and neighbouring parts of Andhra Pradesh, the operative document this week is not the presidential itinerary but the India Meteorological Department's advisories: the system's expected path and intensity will be refined as the low-pressure area develops, and people in coastal and low-lying areas should follow official warnings on heavy rain, strong winds and possible disruption. If the storm's track or timing shifts materially, officials say, the November 4-5 programme could be adjusted again — but as of Saturday, the visit is postponed, not cancelled.
